Development Opportunity
Every piece of land has a story
Netherhouse Mews · Turnditch, Derbyshire

A design-led redevelopment of a redundant former dairy farm, creating four distinctive detached family homes within the beautiful Derbyshire countryside. The scheme reinterprets the site’s agricultural heritage through contemporary barn-inspired architecture, carefully arranged around the established farmyard character and natural topography.

Generous glazing, carefully considered levels and modern rural materials maximise natural light and countryside views while reducing the development’s visual impact. The homes combine strong architectural identity, modern family living and energy-efficient design, supported by enhanced landscaping, biodiversity measures and sustainable drainage.

Four contemporary country homes. One historic farmyard. Reimagined for modern rural living.

Location

Connected countryside, above the Ecclesbourne Valley

Set on Hillcliff Lane on the edge of Turnditch, the site balances a tranquil village-edge setting with genuine connectivity. The A517 links Belper and Ashbourne, with mainline rail at Belper and Duffield placing Derby and Nottingham within easy commuting distance — the profile of buyer that underpins premium village values.

How to bid & what to know

Please read this section carefully before submitting an offer. It sets out the formal bidding process, available technical reports, key assumptions and important notices relating to the site.

The bid deadline will be confirmed — please register your interest below to be notified.

Bids should include details of the proposed financial arrangements and an indicative timetable for exchange of contracts and completion.

Reporting

A suite of technical reports is available on request, including:

Site plans
Topographical survey
Arboricultural Impact Assessment
Design and Access Statement
BNG Strategy
Bat Survey
Drainage Strategy

Bid Process & Assumptions

Bids for the site should be submitted electronically with the subject heading ‘Nether House Farm, Turnditch’ to the F&C Agent via the contact details opposite.
